title: Creating a VM Image Decoy in AWS

blocks.text: Virtual machine (VM) images are used on Amazon Web Services (AWS) to launch new instances of your VMs. You can create a VM image decoy snapshot (public or private) that creates an EC2 instance temporarily in AWS, adds a callback script for detection, and creates a snapshot. Adversaries enumerate public Amazon Machine Images (AMI) with keywords related to your organization in the AMI Catalog with the intention of stealing and accessing the file system by booting up a VM in their environment to extract credentials and exfiltrate sensitive data.

The EC2 instance is created using the t3.small/t2.small series available in the region of deployment. It persists for a duration for 5 minutes and is terminated after the snapshot is built. To learn more about EC2 instance types, refer to the AWS documentation.
Before creating an AWS decoy, you must ensure that you have:

blocks.item: Configured the integration between AWS and Zscaler Deception.
(Optional) Obtained the necessary CloudShell command for deployment script using one of the following methods:
Automated Download Method
Manual Download Method
This only applies to the CloudShell-based deployment.

blocks.heading: Creating a VM Image Decoy in AWS

blocks.text: To create a VM image decoy in AWS:

blocks.item: Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > AWS > VM Image.
Click Add Decoy.
See image.
The VM Image Decoy window appears.
In the VM Image Decoy window:
Name: Enter a name for the VM image decoy.
Account ID: Select the Account ID associated with the AWS account in which you want to deploy the decoy.
Region: Select the AWS region in which you want to deploy the decoy.
Description: Enter a description relevant to the VM image decoy.
Visibility: Select Public from the drop-down menu if you want the VM image to be accessible to anyone. Otherwise, select Private to limit access to the VM image to internal adversaries.

If you want to set the Visibility to Public, ensure that the Block public access for AMIs setting in AWS is disabled in your region of deployment before deploying the decoy. To learn more, refer to the AWS documentation.
Subnet ID: Enable to deploy the decoy in a specific subnet belonging to an existing VPC, then enter the subnet ID.
VPC CIDR: Enter the address in CIDR format for the VPC where you want to deploy the decoy. If a VPC is not available, a new VPC is created. This option is available only if Subnet ID is disabled.
Subnet CIDRs: Enter the subnet IP address range in CIDR format for the VPC. This option is available only if VPC CIDR is configured.
See image.
Click Save.
Deploy the decoy based on the method used to configure the integration between AWS and Deception:
Terraform-based deployment
On the Cloud Deception - AWS page, go to Settings.
Locate the AWS account you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files for is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the aws-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the aws-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of an S3 bucket-based Terraform back end:
{ "terraform": { "backend": { "s3": { "bucket": "your-terraform-state-bucket", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate", "region": "us-east-1", "encrypt": true } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same AWS account.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed, and a JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - AWS page, go to Settings, locate the AWS account you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.
CloudShell-based deployment
Sign in to the AWS Management Console as an administrator.
Click the CloudShell icon on the navigation bar to launch AWS CloudShell.
See image.
The AWS CloudShell window appears.
In the AWS CloudShell window:
Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the automated download method or manual download method.
Enter the option to deploy VM image decoys and press Enter.
The deployment script detects the Account ID and deploys the VM Image decoys to the selected regions.
See image.
If you want to add multiple VM image decoys to AWS, repeat Step 1 to Step 4 for each decoy and then run the script to sync all decoys simultaneously.

Upon successful deployment, the VM image decoy is added to AWS. The deployment status is indicated by the icon next to the name of the decoy in the VM image decoys table (Deceive > Cloud Deception > AWS > VM Image) within the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal. In addition, the Snapshot ID and AMI ID values are automatically associated with the VM decoys. These values are also shown in the VM image decoys table. To learn how to configure lures using VM image decoys, see Configuring Lures Using AWS Decoys.
